title: Compute brief - 27 November 2026
description: Southeast Asia's governments respond to Nvidia's reported shipment pause: Singapore says it cannot confirm it and is tightening anti-diversion checks, while Natixis puts nearly a third of the region's live capacity as China-linked. In the US, CoreWeave's Meta-backed GPU loan prices near 7% while its unsecured bonds yield near 18%. Wire: Singapore response, Malaysia 49.8 GW 2050 demand plan, CoreWeave $4.5 billion Meta-linked loan, FCC Starmind approval, JERA thermal colocation talks, EIA data centre energy survey, Kuwait buys xScale stake, Google Farciennes halt, Telangana 5 GW target, Dutch opposition to MATCH Act, Safaricom 35 MW. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Customer credit sets the price of compute.
lede: A day after the Financial Times reported that Nvidia told Dell, Supermicro and other partners to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said on 27 November the halt has not been confirmed and that Singapore is reviewing its regulations and monitoring so it does not become a conduit for illegal trade. Equinix and Digital Realty played down the impact, but Natixis estimates nearly a third of operational capacity across the four markets is linked to Chinese owners or tenants, above 45% in Malaysia and Thailand. In the US the cost of capital is splitting by customer: Bloomberg reported banks are preparing a $4.5 billion CoreWeave loan backed by its Meta contract at about 7% to 7.5%, while CoreWeave's unsecured 2031 notes yielded near 18% and its five-year CDS hit 15.34%. List prices held for a fifteenth straight tape day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69 and Crusoe's 1 December step-up due Tuesday.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.note: DPM Gan says Nvidia shipment halt not verified; Singapore reviewing anti-diversion regulation and monitoring and engaging the US on chip access for US hyperscalers (Wire, 27 Nov).

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.note: Peninsular power demand projected from 22.6 GW in 2027 to 49.8 GW by 2050, data centres rising from 11% to 21% of load; Natixis says over 45% of live capacity is China-linked (Wire, 26 to 27 Nov).

countries.name: United States
countries.note: $4.5 billion Meta-linked CoreWeave GPU loan at about 7% to 7.5% versus near 18% on unsecured notes (single-source); FCC authorizes SpaceX Starmind; EIA proposes data centre energy survey (Wire, 25 to 27 Nov).

countries.name: Japan
countries.note: JERA in talks with Meta, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and Amazon to site data centres at Tokyo-area thermal plants (Wire, 27 Nov, single-source).

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.note: KIA's Wren House buys GIC's 80% stake in Equinix's European xScale JV, completing Q1 2027 (Wire, 27 Nov).

countries.name: India
countries.note: Telangana targets 5 GW of data centre capacity by 2029 from 300 MW live (Wire, 26 Nov).

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.note: Trade minister urges US not to enforce MATCH Act on ASML and weighs EU countermeasures (Wire, 27 Nov, single-source).

countries.name: Belgium
countries.note: Construction halted at Google's Farciennes campus after work continued on a revoked, water-linked permit (Wire, 27 Nov).

countries.name: Kenya
countries.note: Vodafone plans to triple Safaricom's data centre footprint to 35 MW for sovereign AI and GPU-as-a-service (Wire, 27 Nov).
